questions.q: In Step 1 of the case study, why does the Order status change to 'Ready to Ship' automatically produce an event with no custom publish code?
options: Because Flow always publishes a custom event automatically
Because the WMS polls Salesforce every few seconds
Because Order__c is a platform event object
Because Change Data Capture is enabled on Order__c, and CDC automatically emits a change event on any raw field update
questions.explain: CDC automatically publishes a change event whenever an enabled object's field changes, with no Apex or Flow of yours doing the publishing — exactly the mechanism from Lesson 4.

questions.q: Why does the Apex trigger in Step 2 publish a new `Fulfillment_Requested__e` event instead of letting the WMS subscribe directly to the Order CDC channel?
options: CDC events cannot be subscribed to by external systems at all
Pub/Sub API cannot subscribe to CDC channels under any circumstances
A purpose-built event lets the WMS receive exactly the fields it needs in a clean, stable schema, rather than filtering down a raw CDC payload itself
Custom platform events are always delivered faster than CDC events
questions.explain: Deriving a purpose-built event gives the external WMS a minimal, stable contract — the schema-design trade-off from Lesson 9 — rather than exposing Salesforce's internal Order schema directly across the org boundary.

questions.q: Why does the case study use Pub/Sub API for the WMS's subscription rather than lightning/empApi?
options: Because empApi is deprecated and no longer works
Because Pub/Sub API is required for all CDC events
Because empApi only works with standard-volume events
Because the WMS is an external, non-Salesforce client, and Pub/Sub API is built for exactly that use case, while empApi wraps a connection for code running inside Salesforce's own UI layer
questions.explain: lightning/empApi is for LWCs running inside Salesforce; an external system like the WMS is exactly the client Pub/Sub API was built for, per Lesson 13.

questions.q: Why does the WMS's own subscriber logic need to track which event `id` values it has already acted on?
options: Because Salesforce requires it for billing purposes
Because Pub/Sub API cannot deliver events more than once
Because the WMS has no database of its own
Because at-least-once delivery means the same event could be delivered twice, and reserving inventory twice for one order would be a real, costly duplicate-processing bug
questions.explain: Inventory reservation is not naturally idempotent, so the WMS needs the idempotency tracking pattern from Lesson 10 to avoid double-reserving inventory on a duplicate delivery.

questions.q: What trade-off does the case study acknowledge about adding an Apex trigger in Step 2 to derive a custom event rather than exposing CDC directly?
options: It introduces no trade-off at all; it is strictly better in every case
It eliminates the need for any monitoring in the rest of the pipeline
It removes the need for idempotency handling anywhere downstream
It costs one extra moving part in exchange for a cleaner, more stable schema — defensible here because the subscriber is an external system maintained by a different team
questions.explain: The case study explicitly frames this as a trade-off: an extra component (the trigger) in exchange for schema stability across an org boundary — defensible here, but not automatically the right call in every scenario.
